name: Mixteco de Xochapa / municipio de Alcozauca, Guerrero
confidence_why: 5 independent first-hand descriptions agree (3 state the same rule, 1 refine it); none contradicts.

catalog_quote: Este vocabulario describe el mixteco que se habla en el municipio de Alcozauca, y enfoca especialmente el de Xochapa. ... Las palabras mixtecas se diferencian de las palabras castellanas en que cada vocal tiene su propio tono. Por eso se llama lengua tonal. El mixteco de Xochapa tiene cuatro tonos distintos: alto, medio, casi-bajo y bajo. ... 3.5. Los negativos. La formación del negativo varía con el tiempo del verbo. En el futuro, el negativo se forma con un cambio de tono. Éste es generalmente un desliz ascendente de bajo a alto en la sílaba acentuada (penúltima) y un levantamiento del tono de la última sílaba. koßo 'beberá' kõßó 'no beberá'; sikándå 'moverá' sikãnda 'no moverá'

new_statements.translation: Mixtec words differ from Spanish words in that each vowel has its own tone. That is why it is called a tonal language. Xochapa Mixtec has four distinct tones: high, mid, near-low and low. [...] 3.5. Negatives. The formation of the negative varies with the tense of the verb. In the future, the negative is formed by a tone change. This is generally a rising glide from low to high on the stressed (penultimate) syllable and a raising of the tone of the last syllable. koßo 'will drink' kõßó 'will not drink'; sikándå 'will move' sikãnda 'will not move'

new_statements.relation_note: This work IS the catalog's deciding source (the catalog cites the same 2nd-edition PDF from balsas-nahuatl.org, locator 'Introducción p. V; §0.2 p. 100; §3.5 p. 120'); the catalog quote is confirmed verbatim in the copy opened, and the penultimate placement matches the catalog penultimate stress. Nothing beyond the parenthetical '(penúltima)' is in the work, so it adds no weight, secondary-stress or domain information.
new_statements.rule_in_words: The language is fully tonal (four level tones, every vowel bears its own tone; a few words carry rising or falling glides, and the future negative is marked by a rising glide). The only statement about stress is a parenthetical: the stressed syllable is the penultimate syllable of the word, illustrated on the disyllabic verbs ko'o and sikanda where the negative's rising glide lands on the penult. No dedicated stress or prominence section exists; the tone sections (§0.2-0.3) never mention stress, and 'acento' elsewhere in the sketch means only the acute/grave tone diacritics.
new_statements.exceptions: none for stress placement; 'generalmente' hedges only the shape of the negative tone change, not the location of the stressed syllable. The future/present/preterite tenses are marked by tone on 'la primera sílaba de la raíz' (p. 117-118), which for CVCV roots coincides with the penult. Stress is never claimed to be contrastive.
new_statements.identity_note: Stark et al. describe 'el mixteco que se habla en el municipio de Alcozauca, y enfoca especialmente el de Xochapa' (Introducción p. V), about 8,000 speakers, classed by the authors as Mixteco bajo; this is exactly the catalog's language (alco1235), not another Mixtec variety.

audit.recode_to: Keep penultimate stress (penultimate / right-edge trochee, no secondary stress). Refine the domain note: accent = syllable containing the penultimate MORA of the prosodic word (prefixes + bimoraic root foot); consonant-initial enclitics are adjoined outside and never shift accent (ndu3ba2=ju1 keeps root-initial accent); a prefixed CVV root (ti1kwi14i2) is accented on its word-final long syllable. Re-anchor the deciding citation on Uchihara & Mendoza Ruiz 2022 §3.3 + §5.3.2.1 (with Mendoza Ruiz 2016 p.39 as second source) and move 'fixed-unreviewed' to reviewed.
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote verified verbatim in the SIL dictionary text we hold at pp. V, 100, 120. (2) The deciding source is a basic dictionary's grammar sketch whose only stress remark is a parenthetical '(penúltima)'; Glottolog's top phonology ref (Mendoza Ruiz 2016, 235 pp, instrumental) and the NLLT prosodic-word article by Uchihara & Mendoza Ruiz (2021/2022) are the authoritative descriptions, and both are already held by the project under our earlier reading but are not cited by the catalog record. (3) Read now: both confirm a single right-aligned trochaic foot = accent on the syllable holding the penultimate mora of the prosodic word (root-initial for CVCV roots), no secondary stress, enclitics outside the accent domain — so the penult coding stands, with a domain/mora refinement rather than a reclassify. sources.quote: p.39: 'Así la lengua forma un pie silábico trocaico en bisílabos, es decir, la primera sílaba es fuerte y la segunda débil, mientras que los monosílabos forman un pie bimoraico trocaico.' p.140: glottalization occurs 'siempre en la primera vocal de la palabra, alineada a la izquierda, que es la que suele ser acentuada en Tu'un Savi'. p.143: 'siempre es en la primera vocal del morfema raíz que corresponde a la sílaba prominente de la palabra.' No dedicated stress chapter (thesis is segments + tone); stress treated as root/couplet-initial trochee.
